$comment: RLS-5 gate (scripts/rls-gate.ts). Integration files that still fail under a non-owner Postgres role. THE LIST CAN ONLY SHRINK — the gate fails the build if an entry here starts passing, so a fix must delete its entry in the same commit. Every entry needs a diagnosed `reason`; do not add one to unblock yourself. Read tickets/RLS_HANDOFF.md §7 first.
$baseline: 2026-08-22 — 118 of 124 files pass under RLS_RESTRICTED=true; these are the remaining 6.

allow.reason: 4 failures. The DocuSign webhook (server/routes/esign.routes.ts '/webhook/docusign') is an unauthenticated provider callback with no tenant in context, same shape as the Stripe webhook fixed in 94285423 — envelope creation returns null and the webhook 500s. Needs the same treatment: a bootstrap read that resolves the tenant, then everything else inside withTenant().
allow.followUp: RLS-2f — convert the e-sign webhook path; likely a self-identification clause on signature_requests (0029 already added one) rather than a new migration.

allow.reason: 2 failures. Asserts no temp file is left behind after a timed-out template upload ('expected [ …(4) ] to deeply equal []'), so the cleanup path leaves 4 artifacts. Not yet diagnosed as RLS vs a genuine cleanup bug — the assertion is about the filesystem, not the database, so it may be an unrelated defect this run merely surfaced.
allow.followUp: Diagnose first: confirm whether this also fails in normal mode before treating it as RLS work.

allow.reason: 2 failures, and both are the INVERSE of the usual shape: legitimate actions are being refused (expected 202 got 403, expected 200 got 403). An ACL check is denying a same-tenant operation, which points at an authorization read that lost its scope and now fails closed rather than at row invisibility.
allow.followUp: GH-147 resume/handoff path — check the ACL calls in the resume-link and assignee routes for a missing tx.

allow.reason: 1 failure. 'should allow PUT with valid Bearer token' returns 404 — a legitimate authenticated request finding nothing. Same fail-closed direction as resume-handoff rather than the cross-tenant contract change.
allow.followUp: Likely a fixture with no tenant, or an unconverted read on the PUT route.

allow.reason: 1 failure. 'should generate events and metrics on run completion' — no events are written. Diagnosed: BlockRunner passes `context.versionId ?? 'draft'` into workflow_run_events.version_id, which is `uuid NOT NULL` with an FK — so the literal 'draft' can NEVER insert, and AnalyticsService.recordEvent swallows the error. Under RLS the version fails to resolve, versionId is undefined, and that dead fallback fires. TWO defects: the version resolution (RLS) and the fallback itself, which has never worked in production either — any run without a version silently records zero analytics events.
allow.followUp: Fix the version resolution first; then make the no-version case skip recording explicitly rather than inventing an unstorable id.

allow.reason: 1 failure. 'removes only legacy persisted values when the cleanup migration runs' — the cleanup left extra keys behind. Not obviously RLS-shaped; the assertion is about a config object's contents, so this may be an unrelated defect surfaced by the run.
allow.followUp: Confirm against normal mode before treating as RLS work.
